self_diagnosis.what_went_wrong_1_precedence: v1.0.3's corrected governing rule replaced v1.0.2's two-item allowlist with a hand-enumerated 17-item list. It was STILL a hand-enumerated list, and it still omitted material blocks: v1.0.1's ROTATION_ATTESTATION_EVIDENCE, VERCEL_MEASUREMENT and ALERT_CLOSURE_CRITERIA_AS_AMENDED, and even v1.0.3's OWN NB_CORRECTIONS block. Programmatic enumeration of every top-level key in v1.0.1.json, v1.0.2.json and v1.0.3.json confirms this: v1.0.1 alone has 18 non-administrative top-level keys, and v1.0.3's rule named only 7 of them.
self_diagnosis.what_went_wrong_2_provenance: v1.0.3 presented SEVERITY_ESCALATION_RULE_CLOSED as a discovery of 'the pattern sweep' inside its own hit-classification table. Running the six declared patterns against SEVERITY.escalation_rule's actual text programmatically returns zero matches on all six. The correction itself was right; the claimed method of discovery was not. This is verified by direct regex execution, not by re-reading.
self_diagnosis.what_went_wrong_3_sweep_integrity: v1.0.3 stated the six patterns were 're-run, unmodified' from v1.0.2's SEMANTIC_SWEEP_METHOD.patterns_swept. Byte comparison of the two pattern arrays shows patterns 1-3 changed from `.{0,60}` to `[\s\S]{0,60}?` — a real broadening (cross-newline matching plus non-greedy quantifier), not a re-run of the same patterns. Running the OLD dot-based patterns against v1.0.2's own M-1 old_verbatim citation (which spans a newline) confirms the old patterns would have MISSED it — the broadening was necessary and correct, but was misdescribed as absent.
self_diagnosis.what_went_wrong_4_table_completeness: Programmatically testing every field v1.0.3's table cited against the actual six patterns found the table both OVER-INCLUSIVE (four entries — SEVERITY.escalation_rule, REMEDIATION_REQUIRED.not_sufficient[3], FACTS.F-12, and the .md's M-3 locus — do not match any pattern under exact testing, so they were never real sweep hits, only hand-added because they were correct to discuss) and UNDER-INCLUSIVE (three genuine hits — FACTS.F-11.evidence, SEVERITY.basis.evidence_of_continued_validity, OWNER_DECISIONS.OD-5.why_it_matters — were never listed, though all three turn out to already be covered by S-1, S-4 and S-13 respectively).
self_diagnosis.generalisation: A precedence rule built by hand-listing 'every block I can think of' fails the same way a sweep built by 're-checking the items I was told about' fails: both substitute a curated list for a structural guarantee. The fix in each case is the same shape — flip the default so omission is safe (everything binds unless deliberately excluded; every hit is tested programmatically, not asserted from memory) rather than requiring a perfect enumeration to get the safe outcome.

corrected_rule.mechanism: DEFAULT-BINDING, NOT ALLOWLISTED. Every top-level key in v1.0.1.json, v1.0.2.json, v1.0.3.json and this artifact (v1.0.4.json) confers corrective/controlling force over v1.0.0 (json and md) UNLESS that key appears in the short CLOSED exclusion list below. A new corrective block added in any future amendment is binding by default and requires no separate act of inclusion; only a genuinely administrative key requires an act of EXCLUSION, and that act must be justified here or in a successor.
corrected_rule.why_this_exclusion_list_is_safe: Every excluded key is pure identity/pointer/procedural metadata: none of them ever states a fact about the credential, the alert, or the adjudication's substance. This was verified by reading the actual value of every excluded key across all three amendment files at AS_OF_TREE — none contains a claim about rotation, validity, severity, or any owner decision.
corrected_rule.why_this_does_not_over_include: The remaining ~18-21 substantive top-level keys per file (SECRET_HANDLING_CONTRACT_REAFFIRMED, CERTIFICATION_INPUT/RECERT_INPUT/RECHECK_INPUT, SUPERSEDED_PARENT_CLAUSES, QUALIFIED_CLAUSES_NOT_SUPERSEDED, ROTATION_ATTESTATION_EVIDENCE, VERCEL_MEASUREMENT, REAL_RUNTIME_CONSUMER, CORRECTED_POST_ROTATION_VERIFICATION, EVIDENCE_ACQUISITION_ACTIONS, NEXT_PUBLIC_FINDING, ALERT_CLOSURE_CRITERIA_AS_AMENDED, OWNER_DECISIONS_AFTER_AMENDMENT, MD_PLANE_RESIDUALS_CLOSED, JSON_RESIDUAL_CLOSED, A4_A5_EVIDENCE_REGRADING, DANGLING_IDENTIFIER_CORRECTION, NEXT_PUBLIC_SCOPE_CLARIFICATION, OPTIONAL_CORRECTIONS, SEMANTIC_SWEEP_METHOD/CLASSIFICATION, PRESERVED_PREDICATE_DISCIPLINE, PARENT_BLOB_INTEGRITY, MD_SEVERITY_RESIDUAL_CLOSED, JSON_HISTORY_STATE_TWIN_CLOSED, CHEAP_ADDITIONAL_CLEANUPS, NB_CORRECTIONS, and this artifact's own PRECEDENCE_RULE_STRUCTURAL_REPLACEMENT / SEVERITY_ESCALATION_RULE_PROVENANCE_CORRECTED / SWEEP_METHOD_CORRECTED / MD_OWNER_TABLE_RESIDUALS_CLOSED / NEXT_PUBLIC_LOCUS_CORRECTED / VERCEL_PROJECT_COUNT_REGRADE) are ALL, without exception, either a correction, an evidentiary basis for a correction, or a disclosure about this lane's own conduct (NON_AUTHORIZATIONS). None is a bare quotation of disproven parent text asserted as current — that distinction is handled at the FIELD level by the SUPERSEDED/HISTORICAL_QUOTATION/QUALIFIED/STILL_EFFECTIVE classification already in use, which is orthogonal to and unaffected by this block-level rule. A block conferring corrective force does not mean every sentence inside it is itself a new fact; it means the block's assertions, where they speak to v1.0.0's content, control.

SWEEP_METHOD_CORRECTED.defect: FALSE. v1.0.2's declared patterns 1-3 used `.{0,60}` (a literal dot, which in JavaScript's default regex mode does NOT match a newline character). v1.0.3 actually executed `[\s\S]{0,60}?` for those same three patterns — a character class that DOES match across newlines, made non-greedy in addition. This is a real broadening, not a re-run. Byte comparison of the two pattern-array literals confirms the difference exactly.
SWEEP_METHOD_CORRECTED.why_the_broadening_was_necessary_and_cor: v1.0.2's own M-1 old_verbatim citation ('- **Rotation — unevidenced.** Nothing in this repository attests it, and the\n  alert has stayed open for roughly **2.5 months**.') spans a line-wrap newline between 'the' and 'alert'. Testing the ORIGINAL dot-based patterns against the .md's actual line-wrapped text at that locus returns NO match for pattern 3 across that specific newline boundary the way the broadened version does; the .md's prose is hard-wrapped at ~80 columns throughout, so any locus whose relevant clause straddles a line wrap is invisible to a newline-exclusive pattern. The broadening was the right call. Only the CLAIM that nothing had changed was wrong.
SWEEP_METHOD_CORRECTED.corrected_method_statement: The six patterns declared in v1.0.2's SEMANTIC_SWEEP_METHOD.patterns_swept were BROADENED for patterns 1-3 from a literal-dot form to a `[\s\S]` cross-newline, non-greedy form (patterns 4-6 are unchanged, since a fixed phrase or fixed token cannot itself span a newline in a way `.{0,N}` would miss the way a two-sided proximity pattern can), then run case-insensitively against the full current text of v1.0.0.json, v1.0.0.md, v1.0.1.json and v1.0.2.json. This artifact's own text and v1.0.3's are excluded from being scanned by themselves (a document cannot be swept before it exists) but are checked against the same effective patterns as an internal consistency step; results below.
